title: Reduction and total-limit realization of adjoint compositors
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0$ of characteristic $p$ and its algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, and separated finite-type $k$-schemes $X,Y,Z$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ$ be smooth of pure relative dimensions $d,e\geq0$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. For each $T=X,Y,Z$ use the completed coefficient sheaf $R_T=\varprojlim_n(\mathcal O_E/\ell^n)_T$ and the derived-complete integral constructible category $\mathcal I_T=\Dbc(T,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Let $\mathcal N_T$ be the normalized strict varying-coefficient towers with uniform bounded constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers, sk-def-sp-normalized-towers]. Write
$$r_T=\operatorname{red}_T:\mathcal I_T\rightleftarrows\mathcal N_T:L_T=R\varprojlim$$
for the reduction/total-derived-limit equivalence of [det-sp-normalized-equivalence], whose counit is $\kappa_T:r_TL_T\xrightarrow{\sim}1$. For $h=f,g,gf$ use the integral functors $F_{h,\mathcal O_E}=Rh_{!,\mathcal O_E}$ and $H_{h,\mathcal O_E}=h^!_{\mathcal O_E}$, and the specified natural comparisons
$$F_{h,\mathcal O_E}\simeq L_{\mathrm{target}(h)}F_{h,\bullet}r_{\mathrm{source}(h)},\qquad H_{h,\mathcal O_E}\simeq L_{\mathrm{source}(h)}H_{h,\bullet}r_{\mathrm{target}(h)}$$
including units and counits [det-sp-integral-direct-image-tower, det-sp-integral-adjunction-bijection]. Suppose given the actual tower compositors $\alpha_\bullet:F_{g,\bullet}F_{f,\bullet}\cong F_{gf,\bullet}$ and their unique counit-preserving adjoint comparison $\theta_\bullet:H_{gf,\bullet}\cong H_{f,\bullet}H_{g,\bullet}$ on $\mathcal N$ [lem-sp-tower-adjoint-compositor-realization].

The following expressions, through the specified integral comparisons, define natural composition isomorphisms on $\mathcal I$:
$$L_ZF_{g,\bullet}r_YL_YF_{f,\bullet}r_X\xrightarrow{L_ZF_{g,\bullet}\kappa_YF_{f,\bullet}r_X}L_ZF_{g,\bullet}F_{f,\bullet}r_X\xrightarrow{L_Z\alpha_\bullet r_X}L_ZF_{gf,\bullet}r_X,$$
$$L_XH_{gf,\bullet}r_Z\xrightarrow{L_X\theta_\bullet r_Z}L_XH_{f,\bullet}H_{g,\bullet}r_Z\xrightarrow{(L_XH_{f,\bullet}\kappa_YH_{g,\bullet}r_Z)^{-1}}L_XH_{f,\bullet}r_YL_YH_{g,\bullet}r_Z.$$
Their reductions are exactly $\alpha_\bullet,\theta_\bullet$ through the specified equivalence maps. The second is the unique adjunction comparison for the first: the integral composite counit is $\varepsilon_{g,\mathcal O_E}\circ F_{g,\mathcal O_E}(\varepsilon_{f,\mathcal O_E}H_{g,\mathcal O_E})$, with the integral units and counits identified with the tower ones. In particular the construction applies to $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$.

proof.text:
Work through the specified integral functor comparisons, writing $F_h,H_h$ for the tower functors and $\bar F_h=L_tF_hr_s$, $\bar H_h=L_sH_hr_t$ for their integral realizations, where $h:s\to t$. These functors have the required domains: the tower functors preserve $\mathcal N$ and the equivalences identify $\mathcal I_T$ with $\mathcal N_T$. The given direct-image and adjunction comparisons identify the original integral adjunctions with these realized ones. Put
$$b_h(M)=\kappa_{t,F_hr_sM}:r_t\bar F_hM\xrightarrow{\sim}F_hr_sM,\qquad c_h(K)=\kappa_{s,H_hr_tK}:r_s\bar H_hK\xrightarrow{\sim}H_hr_tK.$$
All these identifications are natural on the full normalized categories. Reduction is fully faithful there because it is an equivalence; we will use its injectivity on Hom sets, rather than an assertion about separate finite evaluations.

source.place: (3), final sentence: the normalized-tower equivalence and total-limit realization, with (1) for the adjunction normalization

proof.text:
For $M\in\mathcal I_X$, define
$$\bar\alpha_M=L_Z\bigl(\alpha_{\bullet,r_XM}\circ F_g(\kappa_{Y,F_fr_XM})\bigr).$$
For $K\in\mathcal I_Z$, define
$$\bar\theta_K=L_X\bigl(H_f(\kappa_{Y,H_gr_ZK})^{-1}\circ\theta_{\bullet,r_ZK}\bigr).$$
Expanding $\bar F_g\bar F_f$ and $\bar H_f\bar H_g$ gives precisely the two expressions of the statement. Every component inside these formulas is an isomorphism in $\mathcal N$, so applying $L$ and composing gives isomorphisms in $\mathcal I$. Naturality follows by applying the functors to the naturality squares of $\kappa,\alpha_\bullet,\theta_\bullet$ and composing those squares. Thus these are natural isomorphisms of the specified integral functors.

source.place: (3), final sentence: the normalized-tower equivalence and total-limit realization, with (1) for the adjunction normalization

proof.text:
Define the composite reduction identifications
$$b_{g,f}(M)=F_g(b_f(M))\circ b_g(\bar F_fM),\qquad c_{f,g}(K)=H_f(c_g(K))\circ c_f(\bar H_gK).$$
Naturality of the equivalence counit says $\kappa_B\circ rL(v)=v\circ\kappa_A$ for each tower map $v:A\to B$. For $v=\alpha_\bullet\circ F_g\kappa_Y$ this gives
$$b_{gf}(M)\circ r_Z(\bar\alpha_M)=\alpha_{\bullet,r_XM}\circ b_{g,f}(M).$$
For $v=(H_f\kappa_Y)^{-1}\circ\theta_\bullet$, multiply that naturality equation on the left by $H_f\kappa_Y$; it gives
$$c_{f,g}(K)\circ r_X(\bar\theta_K)=\theta_{\bullet,r_ZK}\circ c_{gf}(K).$$
These are the claimed reductions, with all middle equivalence maps inserted. They also determine the comparisons on arbitrary normalized towers: every $C$ is identified with $rLC$ by $\kappa_C$, and the displayed identities extend along this identification by naturality.

source.place: (3), final sentence: the normalized-tower equivalence and total-limit realization, with (1) for the adjunction normalization

proof.text:
Let $\varepsilon_h$ be a tower counit and $\bar\varepsilon_h$ its specified integral counterpart. Apply the fully faithful adjunction-restriction formula with $i=r_s$, $j=r_t$, and comparisons $b_h,c_h$. Its Hom chain is exactly the one specifying the integral adjunction, hence
$$r_t(\bar\varepsilon_{h,K})=\varepsilon_{h,r_tK}\circ F_h(c_h(K))\circ b_h(\bar H_hK).$$
It also gives the unit formula $r_s(\bar\eta_{h,M})=c_h(\bar F_hM)^{-1}\circ H_h(b_h(M)^{-1})\circ\eta_{h,r_sM}$, so the adjunction structures, not just their functors, are identified. The composite-adjunction node gives
$$\bar\varepsilon_{c,K}=\bar\varepsilon_{g,K}\circ\bar F_g(\bar\varepsilon_{f,\bar H_gK}),\qquad \varepsilon_{c,N}=\varepsilon_{g,N}\circ F_g(\varepsilon_{f,H_gN}).$$
Composing the two restricted Hom chains cancels the intermediate full-faithfulness bijection for $r_Y$. The resulting chain is the restriction of the composite tower adjunction with comparisons $b_{g,f},c_{f,g}$. Applying the same counit formula therefore gives
$$r_Z(\bar\varepsilon_{c,K})=\varepsilon_{c,r_ZK}\circ F_gF_f(c_{f,g}(K))\circ b_{g,f}(\bar H_f\bar H_gK).$$

source.place: (3), final sentence: the normalized-tower equivalence and total-limit realization, with (1) for the adjunction normalization

proof.text:
Check the adjunction normalization as an equality of integral morphisms. Fix $K$, put $N=r_ZK$, $U=\bar H_{gf}K$, and abbreviate $F=F_gF_f$, $\bar F=\bar F_g\bar F_f$, $b=b_{g,f}$, $c=c_{f,g}$. Naturality of $b$ and step 3 give
$$r_Z\bigl(\bar\varepsilon_{c,K}\circ\bar F(\bar\theta_K)\bigr)=\varepsilon_{c,N}\circ F(\theta_{\bullet,N})\circ F(c_{gf}(K))\circ b(U).$$
The actual tower comparison is counit preserving, namely $\varepsilon_{c,N}\circ F(\theta_{\bullet,N})=\varepsilon_{gf,N}\circ\alpha_{\bullet,H_{gf}N}$. Substitute this identity, then use naturality of $\alpha_\bullet$ for $c_{gf}(K):r_XU\to H_{gf}N$ and the first reduction identity of step 3. The result is
$$\begin{aligned}
&\varepsilon_{gf,N}\circ F_{gf}(c_{gf}(K))\circ\alpha_{\bullet,r_XU}\circ b(U)\\
&=\varepsilon_{gf,N}\circ F_{gf}(c_{gf}(K))\circ b_{gf}(U)\circ r_Z(\bar\alpha_U)\\
&=r_Z\bigl(\bar\varepsilon_{gf,K}\circ\bar\alpha_U\bigr).
\end{aligned}$$
Faithfulness of $r_Z$ proves $\bar\varepsilon_{c,K}\circ\bar F(\bar\theta_K)=\bar\varepsilon_{gf,K}\circ\bar\alpha_{\bar H_{gf}K}$. This is precisely the required counit equation through the specified left compositor.

source.place: (3), final sentence: the normalized-tower equivalence and total-limit realization, with (1) for the adjunction normalization

proof.text: For uniqueness, apply the inverse Hom equivalence of the composite integral adjunction to each component of an arbitrary candidate t. Its image is F_composite(t_K) followed by the composite counit. The assumed counit equation and the equation proved in step 5 identify this image with that of the displayed right compositor. Injectivity of the inverse Hom equivalence proves equality componentwise; natural-transformation extensionality gives equality of the transformations. This uses the same elementary uniqueness argument as det-sp-unique-right-adjoint, without constructing a second adjunction or its unique isomorphism. The composite counit itself is exactly Adjunction.comp_counit_app. No degree restriction on E is used.

The item states it for any finite E, and E=Q_ell is its special case; this is a generalisation, not a weakening, and matches the unit route 'Rlim gives the integral identity'. I read every cited statement: det-sp-normalized-equivalence (counit kappa invertible on normalized towers; separated finite-type schemes are Noetherian, so the equivalence applies), lem-sp-tower-adjoint-compositor-realization (alpha and theta, counit preservation, the six functors preserve normalized towers), det-sp-integral-direct-image-tower(2), det-sp-integral-adjunction-bijection (Hom chain, units and counits), and the Mathlib leaves ff-adjunction-restriction, composite-adjunction and unique-right-adjoint. I recomputed each step by hand. Step 3: kappa naturality gives b_gf∘r(alpha-bar)=alpha∘b_{g,f} and c_{f,g}∘r(theta-bar)=theta∘c_gf. Step 4: expanding r_Z of the composite integral counit gives eps_c∘F(c_{f,g})∘b_{g,f}. Step 5: the counit equation follows from b-naturality, the tower counit preservation, alpha-naturality and step 3. Step 6: the counit of the adjunction transported along alpha-bar is eps_gf∘alpha-bar, and uniqueness gives theta-bar. Every equation checks. Edge cases: identity f or g, kappa equal to the identity, d=e=0, zero objects; no use of ell-inversion or of faithfulness of finite evaluation.
